new_results.statement_exact: **Finite monoids: finite type, finite dimension and bounded homology coincide.** For a finite monoid M: BM has the homotopy type of a finite complex ⇔ of a finite-dimensional complex ⇔ H_k(M; Z) = 0 for all large k; then the universal group U(M) is trivial. Corollaries: a "Swan theorem" for finite monoids (U(M) ≠ 1 forces homology in infinitely many degrees; p-locally too); finite cohomological dimension forces U(M) = 1; with Theorem C of Ben-Bassat (arXiv:2610.38760v1) the homotopy types of finite monoids with bounded homology are exactly the finite simply connected complexes.
new_results.proved_by_exact: The equivalences, U(M) = 1 under bounded homology, and the corollaries: Claude Fable 5.2 (effort max), 12 Nov 2026. Before it: the finite-dimensional case (BM finite-dimensional ⇒ U(M) = 1) is G.4 of the CATHOT return (GPT-6 Astra, effort Pro); the K-theoretic proof of that case through Atiyah's (7.2), (6.11), the route that §§1–2 extend from finite dimension to bounded cohomology, was first written for this problem by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort medium), 11 Nov 2026 (`pro_reviews_20261110/1_CATHOT/REVIEW_G6.md`, route (b)), with the remark that ordinary cohomology does not suffice. The medium review did not state the bounded-homology or finite-type statements.

new_results.statement_exact: **A Kan–Thurston theorem without small quotients, and E.17.** Every connected CW complex W has an acyclic map BG → W such that every homomorphism from G to a group of cardinality < λ factors through π₁(W). Hence a U-small ind-object of Cat_hot is W∞-invariant iff it is ind-isomorphic to an ind-object of groupoids.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The coarse, universal, and local relative classes. Suppose $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal L$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition and pullback. For an arrow $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal M/S$, put \[ u\in W_S^{\mathcal L}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(X\times_S T\longrightarrow Y\times_S T\bigr)\in W \quad\hbox{for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L. \] Let $W_S^u$ be the same class with all $T\to S$ allowed. Then \[ W_S^u\subseteq W_S^{\mathcal L}\subseteq W_S. \] All three classes contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Their retract closure follows if $W$ has it. These are precisely the relative classes in XII ms.~210 and 220. They must not be confused with the class of universal $W$-equivalences in $\mathcal M$, where the base is the codomain of the arrow being tested.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: What raw reindexing and postcomposition actually preserve. Under the hypotheses of A.3, a map $f:S'\to S$ in $\mathcal L$ induces \[ f^*:(\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L}). \] For every $f:S'\to S$, without assuming $f\in\mathcal L$, postcomposition induces \[ f_\#:(\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L}). \] If $f^*$ also preserves the displayed classes, the ordinary adjunction $f_\#\dashv f^*$ descends to their localizations. For arbitrary $f$, this calculation alone constructs the descended postcomposition functor; it does not construct its right adjoint.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The universal saturation of the local test class. Under A.3, define $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ by the following condition on $f:S'\to S$: for every $T\to S$, pullback along $f_T:T\times_S S'\to T$ sends $W_T^{\mathcal L}$ into $W_{T\times_S S'}^{\mathcal L}$. Then $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ contains $\mathcal L$, contains isomorphisms, and is closed under composition and pullback. Moreover \[ W_S^{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=W_S^{\mathcal L} \quad\hbox{for every }S,\qquad \widehat{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=\widehat{\mathcal L}. \] It is the largest composition- and pullback-closed class containing isomorphisms that defines this same family of fine relative classes. This is the corrected, second definition at XII ms.~222; the first definition on that page omits the universal quantifier over $T\to S$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The corrected transporter Galois connection. Let $W$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition in a category $\mathcal M$ with pullbacks. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections. Their extreme pairs are \[ (W^u,\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M),\qquad (W,\operatorname{Fib}_W), \] where $W^u$ means universal equivalences with respect to the codomain of each arrow.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The exact composition criterion, II Proposition 6.1. For a closed pair $A=K_W(L)$, $L=T_W(A)$ of A.6, the following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is composition-closed; pullback along every member of $L$ preserves $A$; and $L=\operatorname{Stab}(A)$, where $\operatorname{Stab}(A)=T_A(A)$. Every stabilizer is composition- and pullback-closed. In particular, a transporter into the larger class $W$ is not generally a stabilizer.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Transporters need not compose under the hypotheses of II section 6. The claim in the first version of II~(6.2)--(6.5) that $T_W(A)$ automatically belongs to a right-hand domain requiring composition closure is false. A counterexample is the chain category $0<1<2<3$, with $W$ consisting of the identities and $0\to2,0\to3$, and $A$ consisting of the identities and $0\to3$. Here \[ T_W(A)=\operatorname{Mor}([3])\setminus\{1\to3\},\qquad K_WT_W(A)=A. \] Consequently $1\to2$ and $2\to3$ lie in the transporter while their composite does not.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The meaning of smooth and proper in the manuscript. For a fundamental localizer on $\mathrm{Cat}$, let $\operatorname{As}_W$ consist of $u:A\to B$ for which $A/b\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$, and let $\operatorname{Coas}_W$ consist of $u$ for which $b\backslash A\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$. The definitions used at II ms.~66 and explicitly reaffirmed at ms.~89 are \[ \operatorname{Liss}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{As}_W), \qquad \operatorname{Prop}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{Coas}_W). \] The two mixed transporters contain both the corresponding stabilizer and $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Neither is the definition of smoothness or properness. The proposed inclusion $\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$ at XII ms.~225--226 is explicitly qualified by ``peut-\^etre'' and is an extra proposed axiom, not a consequence asserted to have been proved there.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The three fibre axioms, with their quantifiers. For every $S\in\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal F_S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal M/S$ on the intrinsic fibrations. The three assertions at XII ms.~215--218 are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{(a)}&\quad J_S:\mathcal F_S[(W_S^u)^{-1}] \longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]\text{ is an equivalence};\\ \mathrm{(b)}&\quad W_S^u=W_S\text{ on }\mathcal F_S;\\ \mathrm{(c)}&\quad\mathcal F_S[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow \mathcal H[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}] \text{ are equivalences} \end{aligned} \] for every full $\mathcal F_S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$. Axiom (a) implies equality of the strong saturations of $W_S^u$ and $W_S$ on $\mathcal F_S$. It does not by that argument imply equality of the original classes. Axioms (b) and (c) imply (a).

dossier_statements.statement_exact: A functorial replacement proves every intermediate-subcategory comparison. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category with a class $W$ containing isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three, let $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A$ be full, and suppose there is $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ with a natural transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal A}\to iR$ whose components are in $W$. For every full $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal A$, both inclusions induce equivalences \[ \mathcal F[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal H[W^{-1}] \longrightarrow\mathcal A[W^{-1}]. \] In particular, such slice replacements into $\operatorname{Fib}_W S$, together with enough intrinsic fibrations, verify XII (a), (b), and (c).

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The two fine axiom systems in XII ms.225--227. Suppose classes $L,P\subseteq\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M$ contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition and pullback. Define $W_S^g=W_S^L$ and $W_S^d=W_S^P$. The clause called (a) on ms.~226, asserting preservation of $W^g$ by $L$-base change and of $W^d$ by $P$-base change, follows formally from the closure hypotheses. The clause called (b) on that page is the additional pair of assertions \[ \begin{aligned} (L/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^d\text{ on }L/S,\\ (P/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^g)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^g\text{ on }P/S. \end{aligned} \] Here $L/S$ and $P/S$ denote full subcategories on the corresponding structural maps. Under these additional equivalences, each fine theory is a contravariant pseudofunctor on all of $\mathcal M$. This conclusion does not require $L\cap P\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The four fibration classes and Loc (7), with reference localizer. For a fundamental localizer $W$, the four classes in XVI section~4 are distinct definitions. Besides intrinsic $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, one has Grothendieck fibrations; $\operatorname{Fib}^{\mathrm{weak}}_W$, tested by all arrows $T'\to T$ over the base with $T'$ and $T$ contractible in the category-homotopy sense; and $\operatorname{Parf}_W=\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W$. Here category-homotopy contractibility means that the identity functor is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations. It implies weak contractibility of the nerve, but replacing the test family by all weakly contractible nerves is a separate assertion, not the literal definition. Let $\mathcal G_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations all of whose transport functors lie in $W$. For any arrow class $\mathcal F$, define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm A(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W,\\ \mathrm B(\mathcal F)&:\quad W_S\cap\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F/S) \subseteq W_S^u\quad\hbox{for every }S,\\ \mathrm C(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\cap W\subseteq W^u. \end{aligned} \] Loc~(7a), (7b), and (7c) are respectively $\mathrm A(\mathcal G_W)$, $\mathrm B(\mathcal G_W)$, and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G_W)$. For a reference localizer $V\subseteq W$, the conditions $\mathrm A_V,\mathrm B_V,\mathrm C_V$ replace $\mathcal G_W$ by $\mathcal G_V$. The condition $\mathrm D_V$ is $\mathrm A(\operatorname{Parf}_V)$, or its equivalent B and C forms once the hypotheses of A.17 are verified. Loc~(7F) is the factorization condition of A.11, not the inclusion of any one of these reference classes in $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The implications A to B to C and replacement transfer. Let $W$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfy A.11's initial assumptions. If every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. If identities lie in $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. Suppose that each $p:X\to S$ in $\mathcal F$ admits a comparison $j_p:X\to R_p$ over $S$ in $W_S^u$, with $R_p\to S$ in $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathrm A(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. If for every map $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ between $\mathcal F$-objects the chosen comparisons extend to a commutative square $R(h)j_X=j_Yh$, then also $\mathrm B(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. Functorial replacements suffice; the proof only needs these individual commuting squares.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The full Brown implication with all its premises. dossier_statements.statement_exact: The local-coefficient repair has an asymmetric conclusion. Let $\mathbb D$ be a derivator in presheaf variance. Suppose that for $p:E\to B$, after every strict base change, the right direct image of every constant coefficient is locally constant and its value at each base object is canonically the right Kan extension from the strict fibre. If $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ is fully faithful on locally constant $\mathbb D$-coefficients, then the pullback $w:E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ is a constant-coefficient $\mathbb D$-equivalence. This argument does not assert full faithfulness or an equivalence on all locally constant coefficients upstairs. If the same direct-image and base-change hypothesis is required for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then the resulting cohomological-fibration class is closed under composition and pullback. The corresponding statements for left Kan extensions and homology follow by duality.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Finite products and the one-fibrant-leg pullback comparison. Assume the hypotheses of A.11 and slice replacement equivalences as in A.12. In the localized fibrant slice over $S$, the product of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ is represented by $X\times_S Y\to S$. Arbitrary derived reindexing preserves these finite products. Moreover, if $X\to S$ is intrinsic and $Y\to\overline Y\to S$ is a replacement with $Y\to\overline Y\in W$ and $\overline Y\to S$ intrinsic, then $X\times_S Y\to X\times_S\overline Y$ lies in $W$. Thus a strict pullback with one intrinsic leg computes the same relative homotopy object as replacing the other leg first. These are the formal assertions at XII ms.~241--248.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The variance assertions of XIII section 4 are lifting adjunctions. Let $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal M)$, suppose the ordinary Kan extensions used below exist, and let the two closed lifting pairs be $(C(I),TF(I))$ and $(TC(I),F(I))$, with $C(I),TC(I)$ defined objectwise. For $u:I'\to I$ one has \[ u^*C(I)\subseteq C(I'),\quad u^*TC(I)\subseteq TC(I'), \quad u_*F(I')\subseteq F(I),\quad u_*TF(I')\subseteq TF(I), \] and \[ \begin{split} u^*F(I)\subseteq F(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!TC(I')\subseteq TC(I),\\ u^*TF(I)\subseteq TF(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!C(I')\subseteq C(I). \end{split} \] If every component of $i\backslash I'$ has an initial object and the relevant coproducts exist, then all four containments in the last two equivalences hold. In particular injective fibrant diagrams are objectwise fibrant. For a walking-arrow diagram $X_0\leftarrow X_1$, injective fibrancy is equivalent to $X_0$ fibrant and $X_1\to X_0\in F$; this also implies that $X_1$ is fibrant.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Closedness upgrades historical exactness to both trivial-class equalities. Let $(C,TC,F,TF)$ satisfy the weak Quillen axioms of XIII ms.~27--28, including two-out-of-three for $W$, the two factorizations, and $TC\subseteq C\cap W$, $TF\subseteq F\cap W$. If both lifting pairs are closed and $W=TF\circ TC$, then \[ TC=C\cap W,\qquad TF=F\cap W. \] Moreover $W$ is retract-closed. With the finite limits and colimits of M0 these data are a closed model structure in the original finite-limit convention. The two intrinsic containments M$''$ make this structure proper. Thus a \emph{closed exact} structure, as required by the uniform hypothesis at XIII ms.~57, is stronger than the unqualified exact structure distinguished in A.22.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The uniform theorem of XIII and the exact admissibility hypothesis. Assume exactly the uniform-left hypothesis of XIII ms.~57: for every $I$ in the specified diagram domain, the objectwise classes $C(I),TC(I)$ and their right orthogonals $TF(I),F(I)$ form a closed exact weak Quillen structure for the objectwise class $W(I)$. Let $u:I'\to I$ be a functor in the domain for which the ordinary presheaf right Kan extension $u_*$ exists. Then $u_*$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrant diagrams. It consequently induces a right adjoint \[ u^*: \mathcal M(I)[W(I)^{-1}] \rightleftarrows\ \mathcal M(I')[W(I')^{-1}]:\mathbf R u_*. \] If the comma categories $I'/i$ and their inclusions into $I'$ belong to the diagram domain, the canonical pointwise formula is \[ i^*\mathbf R u_*X\ \cong\ \mathbf R\!\lim_{(I'/i)^{\mathrm{op}}}X\|_{I'/i}. \] In particular every functor between finite posets is admissible under the source's hypotheses. No restriction to finite posets is necessary for admissibility once the relevant ordinary Kan extension and uniform diagram structures exist. In the historical numbering, this proves the right-hand Der~4 and Der~5 assertions of XIII ms.~61; these numbers do not mean modern Der~4 and strongness Der~5.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The polarity calculation in II section 5 requires closure after a join. For any relation $R\subseteq P\times Q$, the maps $A\mapsto A^\perp=\{q\mid pRq\text{ for all }p\in A\}$ and its transpose define an antitone Galois connection on the power sets. Double orthogonality is an extensive idempotent closure; closed subsets are closed under arbitrary intersections, and their join is the closure of their union. If $P,Q$ are complete posets and the principal-polar condition (D$_0$) of II ms.~69 holds, write $c$ for the induced closure on $P$. For a subset $A\subseteq P$, its polar closure is the principal lower set \[ A^{\perp\perp}=\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee A\right) =\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee_{a\in A}c(a)\right). \] The final closure cannot be omitted from II formula~(5.20), ms.~76. One must also distinguish the element $c(\bigvee A)$ of $P$ from its principal lower set, a subset of $P$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The bi-site remark fixes a question rather than a general theorem. At VI ms.~81--84 the data $(\mathcal M,W)$ specify the coarse slice localization, but the proposed fine classes require additional test data. The two comma tests in $\mathrm{Cat}$ have opposite variances: $X/s$ varies covariantly with $s$, and $s\backslash X$ contravariantly. In XII ms.~222 the class labelled $W^g$ uses the former tests and its universal preservation class is the smooth class discussed in Part B; XII ms.~224's $W^d$ uses the latter. The letters on an earlier page are not a substitute for this variance check. The remark that weak globular infinity-groupoids might have no useful localization theory is a suggestion at VI ms.~83--84. It is not a nonexistence theorem about fine relative theories. The attached 2026 claims about higher categories and globular groupoids remain ``claimed (OpenAI, 2026, unrefereed)'' here \citep{OpenAI2026Thomason,OpenAI2026Groupoids}; no conclusion of Part A depends on either.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The literal absolute package does not imply relative Theorem A. The literal axioms Loc~(1,2,3) of XVI, with the moderate saturation of A.1, do not imply Loc~(3 bis). The failure already occurs in a triangle of finite groupoids over the one-object category $BC_2$. Thus the absolute package left undecided in POLES A.16 must be distinguished from the relative package used throughout the present paper.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The comma tests and their variance. For a fundamental localizer $W$ and a small category $S$, put \[ \begin{aligned} W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S&=\{u:X\to Y\text{ over }S:\ s\backslash u\in W\text{ for all }s\in S\},\\ W^{\mathrm{co}}_S&=\{u:X\to Y\text{ over }S:\ u/s\in W\text{ for all }s\in S\}. \end{aligned} \] Both are weakly saturated classes contained in the total class $W_S$. Opposition gives an isomorphism of relative categories $(\Cat/S,W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)\cong (\Cat/S^{\op},W^{\mathrm{co}}_{S^{\op}})$. For $W=W_\infty$, their enhanced localizations are, respectively, $\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces)$ and $\Fun(NS,\Spaces)$. The value of the first classifier at $s$ is $B(s\backslash X)$; the value of the second is $B(X/s)$. In the notation of XII ms.~222, $W^{\mathrm g}_S$ is the second class.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The simplicial slice test, with the necessary base hypothesis. Let $S$ be a small quasicategory and let $u:X\to Y$ be any map of simplicial sets over $S$; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed fibrant. Then $u$ is a covariant equivalence exactly when \[ X\times_S S_{/s}\longrightarrow Y\times_S S_{/s} \] is a weak homotopy equivalence for every vertex $s$. Replacing $S_{/s}$ by $S_{s/}$ gives the contravariant test. For an arbitrary simplicial base these statements hold with a right, respectively left, fibrant replacement $\widetilde S_{/s}\to S$, respectively $\widetilde S_{s/}\to S$, of the vertex map in place of the literal slice.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Nerve comparison as an equivalence of enhanced localizations. For every small ordinary category $S$, the ordinary nerve induces equivalences \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{co}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq (\sSet/NS)[(W^{\mathrm{cov}})^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS,\Spaces), \] and, by opposition, \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq (\sSet/NS)[(W^{\mathrm{contra}})^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces). \] Here $W=W_\infty$. These are equivalences of infinity-categories and therefore of homotopy categories. The last comparison is implemented by the straightening--unstraightening Quillen equivalence. No model structure on $\Cat/S$ with the ordinary nerve as a right Quillen functor is asserted.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The exact dictionary for smoothness and properness. For $p:A\to B$ in $\Cat$, Grothendieck's $W_\infty$-properness is equivalent to properness of $Np$ in \citet[Definition 4.4.1]{BCCisinski2019}, and to smoothness of $Np$ in \citet[Definition 4.1.2.9]{DGLurieHTT}. Grothendieck's $W_\infty$-smoothness corresponds to Cisinski-smoothness and to the opposite of Lurie's smoothness. Thus the two cited books use opposite names. The equivalences hold in both directions for all ordinary functors, without a fibration hypothesis.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: An explicit smooth and proper path resolution. For a small category $C$ and $x\in C$, let $E_x(C)$ have as objects the functors $\gamma:J\to C$, where $J$ has objects $\mathbb Z$ and arrows $2i\to2i-1$, $2i\to2i+1$, which are constantly $x$ with identity arrows at the left end and constantly some object at the right end. dossier_statements.statement_exact: Cohomological fibrations are not the proper class. Let $\mathcal D$ be the derivator of a nonterminal presentable infinity-category, and use presheaf variance. Define a cohomological $\mathcal D$-fibration by requiring, after every strict base change, that right Kan extension sends every locally constant coefficient to a locally constant coefficient and has the canonical strict-fibre formula. This class and $\Prop_{W_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ are not contained in one another. Dually, the homological class and $\Liss_{W_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ are not contained in one another. In particular both conclusions apply to sets, spaces, and rational complexes.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Intrinsic fibrations for truncation localizers. For $n\geq0$, a functor $p:T\to B$ lies in $\Fib_{W_n}$ if and only if, for every $X\to B$, the canonical map \[ \tau_{\leq n}B(T\times_BX)\longrightarrow \tau_{\leq n}BT\times_{\tau_{\leq n}BB}\tau_{\leq n}BX \] is an equivalence of $n$-types. The pullback on the right is a homotopy pullback in $\Spaces_{\leq n}$. For $n=0$ this is equivalent to the following elementary pair of conditions. For every connected component $B_j$ of $B$, write $T_j=T\times_BB_j$. Then $\pi_0(T_b)\to\pi_0(T_j)$ must be bijective for each $b\in B_j$; and for every arrow $\beta:b\to b'$ and every component $c$ of $T_j$ there must be an arrow of $T$ over $\beta$ in component $c$.

For every spectrum $E$, $\Fib_{W_E}$ contains product projections and inclusions of unions of connected components, together with their closure under composition, strict base change and retracts. For $E\ne0$ this upper bound is strict.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The full fence construction and its mapping-path factorization. Let $\mathcal P(C)$ be the category of all eventually constant diagrams $J\to C$ on the integer fence of B.8, with all natural transformations. Write $\sigma,\beta$ for the eventual left and right values. Then $(\sigma,\beta):\mathcal P(C)\to C\times C$ is smooth and proper for $W_\infty$, and therefore for every fundamental localizer. For every $f:A\to C$, the functors \[ E(f)=A\times_{C,\sigma}\mathcal P(C),\qquad i_f(a)=(a,\operatorname{const}_{f(a)}),\qquad p_f(a,\gamma)=\beta(\gamma) \] give $f=p_fi_f$, with $i_f\in W_\infty$ and $p_f$ smooth and proper. All formulas are natural in strictly commuting squares. For $C=[1]$, the endpoint functor is neither a Grothendieck fibration nor an opfibration. Thus the verified fence construction in PATHS has exactly the asserted homotopical properties, without being a bifibration.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Reversing path words does not repair the all-type endpoint functor. Use the all-type category $\operatorname{Ch}(C)$ with objects finite oriented interval diagrams and morphisms $(h,\eta)$, where $h$ is an endpoint-preserving, weakly monotone functor of their interval types and $\eta:\gamma\Rightarrow\delta h$. dossier_statements.statement_exact: The maximal simplicial classes and the all-base recipe. For every simplicial base $S$, let $W^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ and $W^{\mathrm{contra}}_S$ denote the actual covariant and contravariant equivalences. The maps whose every base change preserves these classes under raw pullback are, respectively, Cisinski-smooth and Cisinski-proper maps. Moreover the manuscript's universal test recipe gives exactly \[ W^{\Liss_{\mathrm{Cis}}}_S=W^{\mathrm{cov}}_S, \qquad W^{\Prop_{\mathrm{Cis}}}_S=W^{\mathrm{contra}}_S. \] Thus opposition gives a perfect duality over $S^{\op}$ for every simplicial base, although B.4 refutes the version using literal slices at an arbitrary base. For accessible $W$, replace fibrewise equivalences of spaces by fibrewise $W$-equivalences after left or right fibrant replacement. These two accessible localizations classify diagrams with values in $\Spaces_W$ on the directed infinity-category presented by $S$ or its opposite, and their restrictions to ordinary nerves are B.16. Their universal raw-pullback classes contain the minimal smooth and proper classes. Complementarity with intrinsic total $W$-equivalences holds for these classes only for $W_\infty$ and the total localizer.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: What a presheaf model supplies before choosing a direction. Let $A$ be any small category, $\widehat A=\operatorname{Set}^{A^{\op}}$, and $i_A X=A/X$ its category of elements. For a fundamental localizer $W$ put $W_A=i_A^{-1}W$. For each $S\in\widehat A$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \widehat A/S\cong\operatorname{Set}^{(A/S)^{\op}}. \] There are two specified, weakly saturated classes on this slice obtained from B.1: \[ W^{\mathrm{pre,el}}_S=i_A^{-1}W^{\mathrm{pre}}_{A/S},\qquad W^{\mathrm{co,el}}_S=i_A^{-1}W^{\mathrm{co}}_{A/S}. \] Both are contained in the total class $W_A$ over $S$. These define localizations for any $A$, but test-category theory alone does not identify them with the two simplicial theories of Part~B.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The extra structure that does transport a duality. Let $M$ have pullbacks and a weakly saturated class $W$, and let $\mathcal L_+,\mathcal L_-$ be two pullback-stable classes. Suppose $D:M\to M$ is an involutive equivalence preserving $W$, together with its canonical pullback comparisons, and carrying $\mathcal L_+$ to $\mathcal L_-$. Then the universal-test classes satisfy \[ D(W_S^{\mathcal L_+})=W_{DS}^{\mathcal L_-}, \] and $D$ induces an equivalence of the corresponding enhanced slice localizations. It also exchanges their universal raw-pullback-preserving classes. Such data are sufficient; being a test category supplies none of the required exchange isomorphisms by itself.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Two strict higher relative theories and a definite duality. For a strict small $n$-category $S$, define $V^{\mathrm{pre}}_S$ and $V^{\mathrm{co}}_S$ by the two slice tests in C.5. They are weakly saturated and contained in the total class $V^{(n)}$. Let $D_{\mathrm{tot}}$ reverse every positive-dimensional cell. Then \[ (n\Cat/S,V^{\mathrm{pre}}_S) \cong(n\Cat/D_{\mathrm{tot}}S,V^{\mathrm{co}}_{D_{\mathrm{tot}}S}) \] as relative categories, and hence their enhanced localizations are equivalent. This conclusion holds for every $1\leq n\leq\omega$ and uses none of the claimed September 2026 model structures.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: What replaces the single opposite in strict dimension $n$. For each subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, or $J\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$ when $n=\omega$, reversing the $j$-cells for $j\in J$ defines an involutive automorphism $D_J$ of strict $n$-categories and preserves $V^{(n)}$. The generators commute and compose by symmetric difference. Define $\Liss^{(n)}$ to be the maps whose every strict base change preserves $V^{\mathrm{co}}$ under raw pullback, and $\Prop^{(n)}$ using $V^{\mathrm{pre}}$. Then both classes contain isomorphisms and are stable under composition and strict base change; $D_{\mathrm{tot}}$ exchanges them. These definitions alone do not identify them with a higher lifting-category criterion or with smooth/proper Street-nerve maps.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The exact coarse consequence of an absolute higher model theorem. Suppose, for a fixed $n$, that the model structure and Quillen equivalence claimed in family~317 are valid \citep[claimed, unrefereed]{OpenAI2026Thomason}. dossier_statements.statement_exact: The formal slice construction. Let $\mathcal M$ be a $\mathbb U$-small category with pullbacks, let $W$ contain the isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three, and let $\mathcal L$ contain the isomorphisms and be stable under composition and pullback. The same assertion holds for a larger category when all the localizations below exist in the chosen larger universe. For $S\in\mathcal M$, put \[ W_S^{\mathcal L}=\{u:X\to Y\text{ in }\mathcal M/S: u\times_S T\in W\text{ for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L\}. \] This class contains isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three, and is contained in $W_S$, the class detected on total objects. If $W$ is closed under retracts, so is $W_S^{\mathcal L}$. Every postcomposition functor $\Sigma_f:\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M/T$, for $f:S\to T$, preserves these classes. If $f\in\mathcal L$, strict pullback $f^{-1}:\mathcal M/T\to\mathcal M/S$ also preserves them and the ordinary adjunction $\Sigma_f\dashv f^{-1}$ descends to both the ordinary and enhanced localizations.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Arbitrary raw pullback does not follow. The hypotheses of E.1 do not imply that raw pullback preserves the fine classes for every $f$. In the presheaf fine theory of $\Cat/[1]$, the inclusion $u:e_1\to[1]$ over $[1]$ is a fine equivalence, whereas its pullback along $e_0\to[1]$ is $\varnothing\to e$, which is not. Consequently the inverse image on the fine localization, when it exists, cannot in general be computed by raw pullback.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: A recognition theorem giving all three Kan functors. Suppose that the enhanced localizations $\mathscr E(S)=(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^{\mathcal L})^{-1}]_\infty$ exist for bases $S$ in a category $\mathcal B$. Suppose we are given a functor $C:\mathcal B\to\Cat_\infty$ with small values and fully faithful functors $h_S:C(S)\to\mathscr E(S)$ satisfying the following precise presentation hypotheses. The category $\mathscr E(S)$ has all small colimits. Each functor $\Map(h_S(c),-):\mathscr E(S)\to\Spaces$ preserves all small colimits. These functors jointly detect equivalences. For each $f:S\to T$, postcomposition descends to a colimit-preserving functor $F_f:\mathscr E(S)\to\mathscr E(T)$ and there is a coherent equivalence $F_fh_S\simeq h_TC(f)$. Then the restricted Yoneda functors give equivalences \[ H_S:\mathscr E(S)\simeq\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces),\qquad H_S(X)(c)=\Map(h_S(c),X). \] Under these equivalences, $F_f$ is left Kan extension along $C(f)^{\op}$; it has right adjoint $f^*$, given by restriction, and this restriction has right adjoint $f_*$. These are coherent functors of the base, hence yield the requested pseudofunctors on homotopy categories. The locally constant subcategory has both adjoints to its inclusion. None of the presentation hypotheses is claimed to follow from E.1 or from factorization through intrinsic fibrations.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Coefficient localization and exact squares. In E.3 one may replace the coefficient category of spaces by any presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, once the slice presentation with those coefficients has been verified. In particular, an accessible reflective localization $L:\Spaces\to\mathcal V$ gives the objectwise localization \[ \Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces)\longrightarrow\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Restriction still has both Kan adjoints, and the locally constant subcategory is reflective and coreflective. For a strictly commuting square of ordinary indexing categories, base change for these Kan functors follows whenever its relevant comma-category comparison is homotopy final for left Kan extension, or homotopy initial for right Kan extension. In particular the presheaf left base-change map is invertible if the vertical map is $W_\infty$-smooth or the horizontal map is $W_\infty$-proper; the right map is invertible with these two roles reversed.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Instances and the extra coarse comparison. For $W_\infty$, the presheaf fine localization of $\Cat/S$ satisfies E.3 with $C(S)=NS$ and $h_S(s)$ the point $e_s\to S$; the dual localization uses $NS^{\op}$. The contravariant and covariant simplicial model structures give the same instances over quasicategorical bases, with the proviso in Part B about raw strict slice tests over arbitrary simplicial sets. For finite Alexandrov posets with downsets open and unrestricted topological total spaces, the open-test localization is the covariant instance $C(P)=NP^{\op}$ proved in Part D. Discrete topological bases give the product of copies of spaces directly. The additional assertion that the coarse localization agrees with the locally constant part requires the coarse comparison \[ (\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\Spaces_{/BC(S)} \simeq\Fun(BC(S)^{\op},\Spaces) \] and compatibility of its localization functor with $\Lan_{q_S^{\op}}$. For $(\Cat,W_\infty)$ this comparison holds. It is not part of the abstract recognition hypotheses.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: What enough intrinsic fibrations supplies. Let $\mathcal M$ have a terminal object and pullbacks, and let $W$ contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Define $\Fib_W$ by universal preservation of $W$ under strict pullback. Assume that every morphism factors as a map in $W$ followed by a map in $\Fib_W$. Then every map in $W\cap\Fib_W$ remains in $W$ after arbitrary pullback. Consequently the full subcategory of objects whose terminal map lies in $\Fib_W$, with these weak equivalences and fibrations, is a category of fibrant objects and presents the same enhanced localization as $\mathcal M$. It supplies finite homotopy limits and the usual homotopy-fibre construction. This does not identify the fine slice theories, and does not imply E.3.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The accessible localizers satisfying the intrinsic factorization axiom. For an accessible fundamental localizer $W$ of $\Cat$, factorization through $\Fib_W$ is equivalent to aspherical generation of $W$, to generation by a set of maps $A\to e$, and to right properness of the associated Thomason model structure. In the corresponding accessible localization of spaces it is precisely nullification. Thus truncation localizers satisfy this factorization axiom; the nonzero-spectrum homology localizers in Part B do not. The right class of the associated modality is not the class $\Fib_W$: every $X\to e$ belongs to $\Fib_W$, whereas a terminal map is in that right class only when its fibre is local.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: What a path object must supply. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has finite limits, $W$ has two-out-of-three, and $\mathcal A=\Liss\cap\Prop$ is stable under pullback and composition and contains product projections. Suppose functorially for each $S$ there is a path object \[ S\xrightarrow{c_S}P(S)\xrightarrow{(s_S,t_S)}S\times S, \qquad s_Sc_S=t_Sc_S=\id_S, \] whose endpoint map belongs to $\mathcal A$ and whose source evaluation $s_S$ is universally in $W$. Then every $f:X\to S$ factors functorially as \[ X\xrightarrow{i_f}X\times_{S,s_S}P(S)\xrightarrow{p_f}S \] with $i_f(x)=(x,c_Sf(x))$ in $W$ and $p_f=t_S\pr_2$ in $\mathcal A$. Merely requiring $c_S\in W$ and $(s_S,t_S)\in\mathcal A$ does not prove the required assertion about $i_f$; the transfer hypothesis must be supplied.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The groupoid test and the meaning of collapse. Let $S$ be a small groupoid and let $\mathcal M=\mathrm{Gpd}$ with categorical equivalences. For functors of groupoids over $S$, both comma-test classes agree with the total equivalences. Their enhanced localizations consequently agree with the coarse theory, which is the infinity-category of families of $1$-types over $NS$. Both variances are identified by inversion in $S$. This does not mean that every artificially chosen class $\mathcal L$ gives the coarse localization.

Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks, let $W$ contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three, and suppose that every arrow factors as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic $W$-fibration. Suppose in addition that for every base $S$ there is a functor \[ R_S:\mathcal M/S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_W S \] and a natural transformation $\eta_S:1_{\mathcal M/S}\to i_SR_S$ whose components are in $W_S$, where $i_S$ denotes the full inclusion. In particular, for every full subcategory $\operatorname{Fib}_W S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$, both inclusions induce equivalences at the restricted $W_S$.

The following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is a nullification; its local objects are closed under dependent sums over local bases, hence form a modality; the canonical map \[ L(X\times_Z A)\longrightarrow LX\times_Z A \] is an equivalence for every $X\to Z\leftarrow A$ with $A,Z$ local; and $\mathcal V$ is locally cartesian closed. Consequently these are additional equivalent conditions in E.8. The modality's left class consists of maps with $L$-contractible homotopy fibres and can be strictly smaller than the class inverted by $L$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The operations supplied by Der 1--4. Let $\D$ be a derivator on all $\mathbb U$-small categories, with presheaf variance, satisfying Der 1--4: coproducts of indexing categories give products, evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms, restriction has both Kan adjoints, and the pointwise comma formulas hold. Then every $f:X\to Y$ has \[ f_!\dashv f^*\dashv f_*:\D(X)\rightleftarrows\D(Y), \] where the display denotes the three functors with their usual alternating directions. For $A\in\D(X)$ and $y\in Y$ the formulas are \[ (f_!A)_y\cong\colim_{(y\backslash X)^{\op}} A, \qquad (f_*A)_y\cong\lim_{(X/y)^{\op}} A. \] The diagram under each limit is restriction along the forgetful functor to $X$, interpreted as a coherent diagram in the derivator. Comma squares are homotopy exact. Exact squares are closed under horizontal and vertical pasting, with the direction of their two-cell fixed. Strongness, pointedness and stability are not needed for these statements.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The two strict base-change theorems and their converses. Consider a strict pullback square \[ \begin{tikzcd} X'\ar[r,"g'"]\ar[d,"f'"']&X\ar[d,"f"]\\ Y'\ar[r,"g"']&Y. \end{tikzcd} \] The canonical maps, with source category $\D(X)$ and target category $\D(Y')$, are \[ f'_!g'^*\longrightarrow g^*f_!,\qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^*. \] The first is invertible if $f$ is $W_\infty$-smooth or $g$ is $W_\infty$-proper. The second is invertible if $f$ is $W_\infty$-proper or $g$ is $W_\infty$-smooth. Conversely, $f$ is proper if its right comparison is invertible for every such square with space-valued presheaves and all coefficients; the dual assertion characterizes smoothness by universal left base change.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The projection formula on the smooth half. Let $\D$ be a symmetric monoidal derivator whose external tensor preserves homotopy colimits separately, in the sense of \citet[Definitions 3.23 and 3.25]{EFGPS2014b}. If $f:X\to Y$ is $W_\infty$-smooth, then for $A\in\D(X)$ and $B\in\D(Y)$ the canonical projection map \[ f_!(A\otimes f^*B)\longrightarrow f_!A\otimes B \] is invertible. More generally this map is invertible for an arbitrary $f$ when $B$ is locally constant. The external formula \[ (f\times\id_Z)_!(A\boxtimes C)\cong f_!A\boxtimes C \] holds for every $f$, every small $Z$, and every $C\in\D(Z)$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The right projection formula and its precise restrictions. For any functor $f$ and any dualizable object $B$ of the monoidal category $\D(Y)$, the right projection comparison \[ f_*A\otimes B\longrightarrow f_*(A\otimes f^*B) \] is invertible. For proper $f$ it is also invertible whenever tensoring with $B_y$ preserves the homotopy limits indexed by $X_y^{\op}$, for every $y$. In a stable monoidal derivator this includes homotopy-finite fibres, for arbitrary $B$. Without such restrictions the right projection formula is false, even for a proper and smooth projection.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Exchange formulas obtained by taking mates. Suppose $\D$ is closed symmetric monoidal. For every $f:X\to Y$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ f_*\underline{\Hom}_X(f^*B,A) \cong\underline{\Hom}_Y(B,f_*A). \] For smooth $f$, put $f^!=f^*$ as the right adjoint of $f_!$. The projection formula then gives \begin{align*} f_*\underline{\Hom}_X(A,f^!B)&\cong \underline{\Hom}_Y(f_!A,B),\\ f^!\underline{\Hom}_Y(B,C)&\cong \underline{\Hom}_X(f^*B,f^!C). \end{align*} The right adjoint mate of the left base-change isomorphism in F.2 is \[ f^*g_*\cong g'_*f'^*. \] All these isomorphisms have the coherence inherited from their specified adjunctions.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Why the adjunction directions reverse. Define the opposite derivator by $\D^\vee(S)=\D(S^{\op})^{\op}$. Then \[ f_!^{\D^\vee}=((f^{\op})_*^{\D})^{\op},\qquad f_*^{\D^\vee}=((f^{\op})_!^{\D})^{\op}. \] Opposition of indexing categories exchanges incoming and outgoing lifting categories, hence exchanges smooth and proper maps. The reversal of the adjunction arrows additionally uses opposition of the coefficient categories. Base opposition alone supplies a comparison of the two fine theories over opposite bases; it is not a duality of coefficients over a fixed base. Nor need $\D^\vee$ be monoidal with a separately cocontinuous tensor.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Open--closed extensions and stable recollement. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow X$ be a sieve and $i:B\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary cosieve. For a pointed derivator there are adjunctions \[ j^?\dashv j_!\dashv j^*\dashv j_* ,\qquad i_!\dashv i^*\dashv i_*\dashv i^! . \] All four Kan extensions are fully faithful; $j_!$ and $i_*$ are extension by zero. In a stable derivator there are coherent fibre--cofibre sequences \[ j_!j^*A\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_*i^*A, \qquad i_*i^!A\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow j_*j^*A. \] Strongness is not needed for these coherent constructions. A triangulated recollement on the ordinary values follows when the stable derivator is strong.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: A correspondence formalism on the smooth class, with an enhancement. Let $\mathcal V$ be a $\mathbb V$-presentable closed symmetric monoidal infinity-category whose tensor preserves $\mathbb U$-small colimits separately. Regard the ordinary category $\Cat_{\mathbb U}$ as an infinity-category by its nerve, so its pullbacks are the strict categorical pullbacks. Put $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$. There is a lax symmetric monoidal functor \[ \Corr(N\Cat_{\mathbb U})_{E,\mathrm{all}} \longrightarrow\Cat_{\infty,\mathbb V},\qquad S\longmapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\mathcal V), \] sending a span $X\xleftarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}Y$, $b\in E$, to $b_!a^*$. It is a pre-six-functor formalism in \citet[Definitions A.5.1 and A.5.6]{EFMann2022} and a six-functor formalism in Definition A.5.7 there. The restriction to homotopy categories is the indicated half of the represented derivator. This assertion uses the given infinity-category, not merely its valuewise homotopy categories.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The terminology of the resulting operations. In F.10 every allowed map has $f^!=f^*$ and $f^!\one=\one$, compatibly with base change. Thus all these maps satisfy the cohomological smoothness formula with the trivial invertible twist; in the usual terminology for this identity they are cohomologically \emph{\'{e}tale}. This does not say that a Grothendieck-proper functor has $f_!=f_*$. Even a functor belonging to both Grothendieck classes need not have this ambidexterity. For a discrete bifibration with finite fibres, however, a stable coefficient category has the canonical ambidexterity $f_!\simeq f_*$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: H\"ormann's diagram correspondences and the enhancement boundary. Fibered multiderivators encode the two halves and their exchange maps on the appropriate 2-multicategory of diagram correspondences. In \citet[Theorem 6.12]{EFHormann2017}, for pre-multiderivators $\mathbb E,\mathbb S$ satisfying Der 1--2, a strict morphism $\mathbb E\to\mathbb S$ is a left, respectively right, fibered multiderivator precisely when the induced map $\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb E)\to\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb S)$ is a 1-opfibration, respectively 1-fibration, of 2-multicategories. A closed monoidal derivator supplies the associated diagram-level six-operation structure. This does not turn all strict pullback squares of ordinary categories into exact squares and does not itself construct an infinity-categorical enhancement of an abstract derivator.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The genus-zero category and its geometric coefficients. For $n\geq3$, let $\Gamma_n$ be the pure orientation-preserving mapping class group of the $n$-punctured sphere. Let $\mathcal C_n$ have as objects the isotopy classes of essential multicurves, including the empty multicurve, and put \[ \Hom_{\mathcal C_n}(\sigma,\tau) =\{g\in\Gamma_n:g\sigma\supseteq\tau\}/\Delta_\sigma, \qquad [h]\circ[g]=[hg], \] where $\Delta_\sigma$ is generated by the Dehn twists in the curves of $\sigma$ and acts on the right. Set $T_{0,n}=\mathcal C_n^{\op}$. The exit category of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$ with its dual-tree stratification is $N\mathcal C_n$. For every compactly generated presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, \[ \Shv_{\mathrm{cbl}}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C);\mathcal V) \simeq\Fun(N\mathcal C_n,\mathcal V) =\Fun(NT_{0,n}^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Forgetting the last mark induces $Q:\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$, $\sigma\mapsto q\sigma$, $[g]\mapsto[\phi(g)]$, and $F=Q^{\op}:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$. Here $q$ erases curves which become peripheral and identifies repeated isotopy classes, and $\phi:\Gamma_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma_n$ is the forgetful homomorphism.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Indexing an abstract derivator by strict higher categories. For a specified extension of an ordinary derivator to strict $n$-categorical indexing shapes, $2\leq n\leq\omega$, with lax or colax comma objects and a chosen Street-nerve weak-equivalence class, does the corresponding universal smooth/proper lifting condition imply the two base-change isomorphisms of F.2, with coherent mates? We have not established this statement. Even $n=2$ requires an explicit higher Der~4 and an invariance theorem for the chosen lax comma construction; neither is part of an ordinary derivator on $\Cat$. The model-structure claim discussed in Part C supplies neither datum. No proof in Part F uses that unrefereed claim.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: An exact proper class in the diagonally closed setup. In the discrete-fibration setup of F.12, take $\mathcal V=\Sp$ or $D(k)$ for a nonzero commutative ring $k$. dossier_statements.statement_exact: The exact stability input and the available tensor action. dossier_statements.statement_exact: The canonical dualizing weight and its exact variance. Let $S$ be homotopy finite. Write \[ R_s(t)=\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_S(t,s),\qquad w_S(s)=\lim_{t\in S^{\mathrm{op}}}R_s(t). \tag{G.2a} \] Then $w_S:S\to\mathrm{Sp}$ is a covariant spectral diagram, with finite-spectrum values, and for every stable derivator there is a canonical natural isomorphism \[ p_*^S F\simeq w_S\otimes_{[S]}F =\int^{s\in S} w_S(s)\otimes F(s). \tag{G.2b} \] The integral denotes the derived coend, with its coherent spectral action. It is not an objectwise tensor followed by the ordinary colimit over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The exact canonical equivalence criterion for finite posets. For a finite poset $P$ define the colimit-preserving transform \[ (V_PF)(s)= \lim_{t\in P^{\mathrm{op}}} \bigl(\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_P(t,s)\otimes F(t)\bigr), \qquad V_P:\mathbb D(P)\longrightarrow\mathbb D(P^{\mathrm{op}}). \tag{G.9a} \] There is always a canonical formula \[ p_*^P\simeq p_!^{P^{\mathrm{op}}}V_P. \tag{G.9b} \] For spectra the transform (G.9a) is an equivalence if and only if each strict upper interval $P_{>p}$ is Gorenstein* over $\mathbb Z$. Here a finite poset $L$ is Gorenstein* when every open interval in $L$ with a newly adjoined bottom and top has the integral homology of a sphere; the empty interval is allowed as the $(-1)$-sphere. When this condition holds, (G.9a) gives an equivalence for every stable derivator, and it restricts to pointwise finite spectra or perfect complexes. This is a condition on this canonical transform; it is not a classification of every possible equivalence between the two diagram categories.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Verification of the finite least-vertex geometric dictionary. Let $P$ be a finite poset and $Z=\|NP\|$. Label a point by the least vertex with positive barycentric coordinate. With downsets open on $P$, this is a continuous map $s:Z\to P$; its strata are contractible, the stratification is conical, and its exit-path infinity-category is $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Consequently \[ \operatorname{Shv}_{P\text{-}\mathrm{cons}}(Z;\mathcal C) \simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C) \tag{G.10} \] for spaces, for every compactly assembled coefficient infinity-category, and for every stable presentable coefficient infinity-category. The inverse-image functor from sheaves on the finite downset Alexandrov space $P$ is the fully faithful functor onto the subcategory in (G.10).

dossier_statements.statement_exact: A correct geometric Verdier identification with a checked hypothesis. Suppose the finite poset $P$ satisfies the upper-interval criterion of G.9. For $Z=\|NP\|$ and its minimum map $s:Z\to P$, the spectral transform has the identification \[ V_P\simeq s_+\,\mathbb V_Z\,s^*. \tag{G.12} \] Here $\mathbb V_Z$ is Lurie's covariant sheaf--cosheaf duality and $s_+$ is cosheaf pushforward, with value on $U$ given by the value on $s^{-1}U$. The same identification holds for derived coefficients over a ring. Thus it includes an explicit pushforward of cosheaves; it does not require the ordinary sheaf-valued Verdier dual to stay constructible for the same minimum strata. A concrete class satisfying the criterion is $P=\operatorname{Face}(K)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for any finite simplicial complex $K$, with nonempty faces. In this case the minimum strata on the barycentric subdivision are precisely the open simplices of $K$, so the identification is the usual cellular geometric one.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: An elementary quotient of the homotopy category. Let $\mathscr K$ be the homotopy category of CW homotopy types, and fix $K=S^1$. Let $I(X,Y)$ be the set of homotopy classes $X\to Y$ factoring through $K$. There is a category $\mathscr Q$ with the same objects and \[ \mathscr Q(X,Y)=\bigl(\mathscr K(X,Y)\amalg\{0\}\bigr)/ \bigl(I(X,Y)\sim0\bigr). \] For the quotient functor $q:\mathscr K\to\mathscr Q$, the morphism $q(f)$ is invertible exactly when $f$ is invertible in $\mathscr K$, or both its source and target are homotopy retracts of $S^1$. Those retracts have homotopy type $e$ or $S^1$.

The complete list of settled and unresolved named assertions is \texttt{sections/BC\_historical\_audit.csv}. B.11--B.14 below settle the formal decomposition statements, finite localization statements, the two discrete-set adjunctions, and the elementary cube implications. The remaining unresolved assertions include the infinite-product generality of Lemma~2.5 after adding identities, the variants with the full decomposition hypothesis in XV~9.7 and 9.11, and the full Mayer--Vietoris implications in XVI~3.2--3.7. B.17 refutes several of the other nontriviality equivalences under the literal absolute axioms. Replacing absolute Loc~(3) in D\'efinition~1.1 by relative Loc~(3 bis) repairs the product argument in B.8; the separate correction in B.11 is still needed. Optional axioms Loc~(4)--(8) retain their stated hypotheses. | claim (return: Open) |  |

dossier_statements.statement_exact: A weak localizer with near-bijective infinite component maps. Call a map of sets $f:I\to J$ a near bijection if there are finite subsets $I_0\subset I$ and $J_0\subset J$ such that its restriction $I\setminus I_0\to J\setminus J_0$ is a bijection. Define, on all small categories, $W_{\mathrm{nb}}$ by the following two alternatives: \[ \begin{split} u:A\to B\in W_{\mathrm{nb}}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad& \bigl(\pi_0A,\pi_0B\text{ finite and }u\in W_\infty\bigr)\\ &\text{or }\bigl(\pi_0A,\pi_0B\text{ infinite and } \pi_0u\text{ a near bijection}\bigr). \end{split} \] This class satisfies literal Loc~(1), Loc~(2), absolute Loc~(3), and closure under finite coproducts. Its aspherical categories are exactly the weakly contractible categories. There are distinct parallel arrows in its localization even though it contains maps which are not bijective on components.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Universal weakness and fibrewise invariance. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has pullbacks, $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three, and every map factors as a map in $W$ followed by an intrinsic fibration. Then \[ W\cap\operatorname{Fib}_W=W^u. \] Moreover every $W$-map between intrinsic fibrations over $S$ remains weak after arbitrary change of base. Thus XII axiom (b) follows.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Lead 3 without functorial factorization. Under C.1's hypotheses, for every full subcategory \[ \mathcal F_S:=\operatorname{Fib}_W S\ \subseteq\ \mathcal H\ \subseteq\ \mathcal M/S \] the inclusions induce equivalences on ordinary localizations and on $\infty$-categorical localizations at the restricted $W_S$. Consequently factorization alone implies all three axioms (a), (b), (c). No global terminal object, functorial factorization, retract closure, or strong saturation of $W$ is required.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The proper-localizer criterion, including its local form. For $n\geq0$, put $W_n=\{u:\tau_{\leq n}Bu\text{ is an equivalence}\}$. A functor $p:E\to B$ belongs to $\Fib_{W_n}$ if and only if every strict pullback square along $X\to B$ becomes a homotopy pullback after applying $\tau_{\leq n}B(-)$. Equivalently, it suffices to require this for all $X$ having a terminal object. Another equivalent test is that, for every triangle $X\to Y\to B$ with $X$ having a terminal object and $BY$ $n$-connected, the functor $E\times_BX\to E\times_BY$ belongs to $W_n$. For $p\in\Liss_{W_n}$ or $p\in\Prop_{W_n}$, it suffices to test the squares along the objects $b:*\to B$.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Lead 1 is true. Suppose $p:E\to B$ is a small-category functor such that, for every $X\to B$, the canonical map $B(E\times_BX)\to BE\times^h_{BB}BX$ is a weak equivalence. For $n\geq1$, it belongs to $\Fib_{W_n}$ if and only if every connecting homomorphism \[ \partial_b:\pi_{n+1}(BB,b)\longrightarrow\pi_n(BE_b,x) \] is zero, for every $b$ and every vertex $x\in E_b$. For $n=0$, the criterion is that the monodromy action of $\pi_1(BB,b)$ on $\pi_0(BE_b)$ is trivial. Empty fibres and components outside the image of $BE$ are allowed.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The coefficient tests and their variance. For a nonzero commutative ring $k$, a functor $u:A\to B$ lies in $W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}}$ exactly when it is bijective on components, induces isomorphisms on $\pi_1$ at all basepoints, and induces $k$-homology equivalences of the simply connected universal covers of corresponding components. Consequently $W_{D(\mathbb Z)}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_\infty$. For $k=\mathbb Q$ the higher test is $\pi_i(Bu)\otimes\mathbb Q$ being an isomorphism for every $i\geq2$. For sets and groupoids as coherent coefficients, the locally constant classes are $W_1$ and $W_2$, respectively.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Rational local coefficients require only the degree-two boundary. Under the homotopy-pullback hypothesis of D.2, $p:E\to B$ belongs to $\Fib_{W_{D(\mathbb Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ if and only if every boundary $\pi_2(BB,b)\to\pi_1(BE_b,x)$ is zero. There is no vanishing condition on the higher rational boundaries. In particular the stronger proposed test in Part D(3) is false.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The remaining coefficient classification. For arbitrary functors without the hypothesis of D.2, a comparable explicit fibre criterion for $\Fib_{W_{D(\mathbb Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ is not established here. Nor do we establish a complete characterization of $\Fib_{W_{D(\mathbb F_p)}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$, even among the homotopy-pullback functors of D.2. The integral, set, and groupoid cases reduce exactly to $W_\infty,W_1,W_2$ by D.5. Merely declaring higher boundary maps zero after tensoring with a field is not a proof of the unresolved mod-$p$ case: integral fundamental groups are retained by that coefficient localizer.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: A connected intrinsic homology covering need not be trivial. Let $p$ be a prime. Any categorical covering whose monodromy factors through a finite $p$-group belongs to $\Fib_{W_{H\mathbb F_p}}$. dossier_statements.statement_exact: Trivial monodromy is necessary and sufficient for integral and rational homology. Let $p:E\to B$ be a categorical covering, that is, a discrete fibration and discrete opfibration. For either $k=\mathbb Z$ or $k=\mathbb Q$, it belongs to $\Fib_{W_{Hk}}$ if and only if its monodromy on every fibre set is trivial. Equivalently, over each connected component $B_0$ it is isomorphic to a product $B_0\times S_0\to B_0$, where $S_0$ may be empty or infinite. In particular a nonempty connected covering of a connected base is intrinsic for either of these two homology localizers exactly when it is isomorphic over the base to its identity covering. This assertion is specific to these coefficients; D.8 gives the contrary mod-$p$ behavior.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The action criterion used in this part. Here total asphericity means the condition of XII ms.~88 tested by all ordinary final images; we do not substitute the different diagonal-asphericity terminology used elsewhere in the literature. For a nonempty connected small category $A$, total $W_\infty$-asphericity is equivalent to every connected component of $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ being weakly contractible, for every covariant $H:A\to\mathrm{Set}$. It is also equivalent to the same condition with integral acyclicity in place of weak contractibility. Exactness of $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ implies these conditions.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The requested injection and free-category examples. Let $A_S$ be the full subcategory of $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ on $[n]$, $n\in S\subseteq\mathbb N$. It is totally $W_\infty$-aspherical exactly when $S$ is a singleton or unbounded. In these cases its integral colimits are exact. The category of finite sets and injections, with or without the empty set, is not totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. The one-object category of injective self-maps of $\mathbb N$ is not totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. For the free category on any small directed graph, total $W_\infty$-asphericity is equivalent to filteredness; local finiteness is unnecessary.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The exact connected converse. For a nonempty connected small category $A$ with no weakly terminal object, we do not settle whether total $W_\infty$-asphericity forces exactness of $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$. The exact gap is whether the hypotheses of F.2 equalize every parallel pair in $\operatorname{Aff}_{\mathbb Z}(A)$, not merely every original parallel pair. F.3 resolves the listed injection and free-category candidates but does not remove this gap for a general countable category. Exact integral colimits remain a proved sufficient condition, and the affine-filtered criterion is the precise algebraic reformulation. The original claims of equality with filteredness are false by the unbounded $A_S$ examples.

The proof of F.1 does not transfer: for a presheaf $H$ on $A$, totality tests only those covariant actions on its element category pulled back from $A$, whereas the cyclic-cover argument needs arbitrary actions on that element category. dossier_statements.statement_exact: Universal Cat-colimit shapes without a weakly terminal object. For a connected countable category $I$ without a weakly terminal object, and hence also in general, the implication from the universal ordinary-Cat-colimit comparison to filteredness remains unresolved here. F.4 gives a necessary totality condition and the full weakly-terminal case. The unbounded injective-ordinal examples do not refute this implication: the diagram $[n]\mapsto B\mathbb N^{n+1}$ has categorical colimit $B\mathbb N\simeq S^1$, whereas its Grothendieck construction has integral homology $\mathbb Z$ in every degree. On all of $\Delta_{\rm inj}$ its degree-$k$ fibre homology, for $k\geq1$, is the projective representable $\mathbb Z[\Delta_{\rm inj}([k-1],-)]$; the homotopy-colimit spectral sequence collapses. On an arbitrary unbounded full subcategory $A_S$, the restricted diagram need not be representable. Instead its higher derived colimits vanish by exactness in F.3, and its colimit is $\mathbb Z$: any two marked $k$-element ordered subsets admit embeddings into a common larger ordinal identifying their marks, then into an object of $A_S$. The categorical colimit is still $B\mathbb N$, since the same embeddings identify all coordinate generators and introduce precisely their commutative-monoid relation. Thus all these shapes fail the premise. This prevents importing the nonfiltered total example as an answer to the different Cat-colimit question.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: Let $p:E\to B$ be a functor of ordinary small categories, and form its strict diagonal $\Delta_p:E\to E\times_B E$. Then \[ p\text{ and }\Delta_p\text{ are }W_\infty\text{-smooth} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p\text{ is a discrete fibration}. \] Consequently the discrete fibrations form the largest subclass of $\operatorname{Liss}_{W_\infty}$ closed under diagonals. They are also closed under identities, composition and strict pullback.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The preceding proof does not follow from \citet[Proposition A.5.10]{GHIJMann2022} by taking $I$ to be all smooth maps and $P$ to be the isomorphisms. That specialization violates the suitable-decomposition cancellation requirement. Indeed $p:[1]\to*$ and $pg:*\to*$, where $g$ selects $1\in[1]$, are smooth, but $g$ is not smooth: the incoming arrow $0\to1$ has no lift. Thus $p,pg\in I$ does not imply $g\in I$. The span universal property used in I.3 is the needed replacement. Contractible uniqueness of individual adjoints, without this extension statement or an explicit unfurling construction, by itself does not state the necessary coherence theorem. The program \texttt{code/GHIJ/small\_counterexamples.py} enumerates the incoming lifts for $p$, $pg$, and $g$, verifying this finite cancellation counterexample.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: For spectra or $D(k)$, with $k$ a nonzero field, the universally ambidextrous discrete fibrations are precisely the finite discrete bifibrations: their fibres are finite sets, and all reindexing functions along base arrows are bijections. Together with I.2 and I.6 this gives the unstable and stable proper-map classifications within the maximum diagonal-stable class. dossier_statements.statement_exact: The second stages for spectra and mod-$p$ coefficients. Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal U$, and use a larger universe for categories of $\mathcal U$-small objects. Let $\mathcal C$ be either $\operatorname{Sp}_{\mathcal U}$ or $D(\mathbb F_p)$, with its indicated presentable infinity-category enhancement. We number the stages by \[ W_{\mathcal C}^{(0)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \mathcal C_1=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}^{\mathrm{lc}}. \tag{I.9.1} \] Here $\mathcal S_W$ is the accessible reflective localization of spaces at exactly the class $W$, and $\mathbb D_{\mathcal E}(A)=\operatorname{Ho}\operatorname{Fun}(NA^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)$. The localizations in (I.9.1) exist and preserve finite products. Their constant-coefficient classes satisfy $W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}$. For every map $u:X\to Y$ of small spaces, \[ u\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective and } \Omega_xu\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}. \tag{I.9.2} \] The loop condition is tested at one basepoint in every component of $X$. Consequently \[ W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(1)} =W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(2)}=W_\infty, \tag{I.9.3} \] and \[ u\in W_{D(\mathbb F_p)}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_i(u)\text{ is an integral isomorphism for }i=1,2,\\ H_*(u\langle2\rangle;\mathbb F_p)\text{ is an isomorphism}. \end{cases} \tag{I.9.4} \] For a pointed connected component, $X\langle2\rangle$ means the homotopy fibre at its chosen basepoint of $X\to\tau_{\leq2}X$. The map $u\langle2\rangle:X\langle2\rangle\to Y\langle2\rangle$ is induced by $u$ and the basepoints. The last two conditions of (I.9.4) are tested on every corresponding pointed component. There are no nilpotence or finite-type hypotheses. The second class is again accessible and product stable, so $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}}$ realizes it as an ordinary constant-coefficient class. This construction can be iterated at every finite stage for these two starting coefficients. It is a specified realization by localized spaces; functorial construction on all bare derivators and all exact morphisms remains the separate Open assertion of I.7.

dossier_statements.statement_exact: The universally pullback-preserving classes in Part J(2), the complete boundary-piece tests, and the proposed lax-comma Der~4 base-change theorem in J(3) are not established here. The absolute model structure and Theorem A do not imply those claims. The verified statements available from the sources are Theorem A for the specified slices \citep[Theorem 5.2]{GHIJAraMaltsiniotis2018} and invariance under every cell duality \citep[Theorem 6.6]{GHIJAraMaltsiniotis2022}. A full four-variance base-change table requires the still-missing recognition and lax-comma compatibility.
